parsed.why: No criminalisation and courts have granted trans relief, but recent reporting documents discrimination in public spaces and state institutions plus physical/sexual harassment of visibly trans people, with hostile political rhetoric and thin recourse.

State threat-framing (LGBTQ listed among national-defence risks), penal code reaching same-sex conduct, public canings, police raids, vigilante mobs attacking trans women, and a trans traveller's death in custody.
No criminalisation and working document reform, but border officers stop male-marker holders, hate-crime law omits gender identity, society stays conservative; documented violence is old (2012).

No criminalisation, no border LGBT screening, constitutional court struck down anti-LGBT minors law; negatives are resident-sphere (workplace bias, assembly policing) plus conservative hostility, with no documented trans-targeted violence.
No criminalisation and cooperative official posture, but documented police extortion and abuse of trans women, a street-harassment pattern, a dated arrest survey, and no working remedies.
